payload.title: Anth.us-Papyrus: exact front-end parity with the production Anth.us site (site-side work)
payload.description:
## Goal The Anth.us-Papyrus port's front end must look **exactly** like the existing production Anth.us site. Ryan: *"We want the front end design to be exactly the same as the old site."* And later, lifting an earlier constraint: *"Yes, fix Markus"* — where Markus's markup or design language blocks parity, fix it upstream in Papyrus/Markus, publication-neutral and config-driven, rather than doing regex surgery in the site build. Ryan accepted explicitly that this means the site stops using Markus's own layout/design language. That decision is settled; do not re-litigate it. ## Diagnosis (established — do NOT re-derive) The two sites share **ZERO** CSS class names. | | Production | The port, before this work | | --- | --- | --- | | Classes | index-module--listItem--06e6d, index-module--postsListItem--87ad2, blog-post-preview, gatsby-image-wrapper, clear-float, right, date, button, logo | markus-card, markus-card-grid, markus-document, markus-site-masthead, markus-site-nav, markus-header, markus-lede, markus-two-up | | CSS | 33KB SCSS -> 26,104-byte compiled bundle (Gatsby CSS-module hashed names) | hand-written 12,241-byte web/css/anthus-theme.css | That is the whole cause of the layout differences. Tuning the 12KB file never converges. Ground truth: /Users/home/Projects/Anth.us/public/ — a real 2026-09-24 Gatsby production build, 243 rendered HTML pages plus styles.04b540856f53bb5e70f2.css. READ-ONLY and precious. ## Branch / worktree / PR - Branch: feature/exact-design-parity (pushed), off feature/anthus-papyrus-port - Worktree: /Users/home/Projects/Anth.us-Papyrus-design - Commit: 14b0adf "WIP: ship the production Anth.us stylesheet and DOM layer" - **No PR opened** — the build does not currently run. - **READ web/WIP-DESIGN-PARITY.md FIRST.** It is the full handoff: what is done, what is half done, the exact pick-up points, and the findings. ## Depends on the Markus/Papyrus work Blocked-ish on PPY-5aee133c-b07a-470f-a3f2-21abc349fd39 (branch feature/markus-layout-parity, worktree /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-design, commit fcd84d9fa69eb9091578820823fda7ecf1b60ce3, no PR). That branch adds the configurable page shell this site build is meant to consume instead of monkeypatching papyrus_content.markus_renderer.shell.render_page. See also PPY-6ee6aa — reference-side analysis for web/anthus_page_html.py (the four static pages: about, ai-solutions, ryan, 404). No code was written for it; the analysis is worth reading before starting. ## THE BUILD IS CURRENTLY BROKEN web/anthus_mdx.py now emits image / / is swapped. A small staging notice is appended inside the footer's dark band (AGENTS.md requires a visible non-production marker) — that is an intentional, documented difference. | ## Per-page parity: NOTHING VISUALLY VERIFIED **No page has been rendered or screenshotted on the new build.** Zero pages can be reported as visually matching. Every claim above is structural (selector-set equality and DOM comparison against the reference HTML), which is exactly the weaker form of evidence that misled the previous two agents. The harness is built and self-tested, so this is the cheap first step: bin/shoot.js (Puppeteer) + bin/compare.py (Pillow, mean abs pixel diff, >16 threshold percentage, side-by-side and heatmap output, plus a per-page class-token diff and docHeight delta). Self-test against Anth.us/public served on 8081: same-directory comparison pixel-identical; two independent runs differ by a single antialiasing pixel. Two environment facts that cost time to find: - Puppeteer is at /Users/home/Projects/Pilobol.us/node_modules/puppeteer (v25.10.0). It is NOT under Anth.us, contrary to the original brief. - Puppeteer's managed Chrome was never downloaded (~/.cache/puppeteer absent), so a plain puppeteer.launch() FAILS. shoot.js resolves the Playwright-managed chrome-headless-shell instead. ## Findings worth keeping - **Production platform-product pages are BROKEN.** /platform//index.html renders with NO chrome at all — no .layout, no header, no footer, just the MDX body. Same for /solutions// and the bare-slug article duplicates (/ai-agents/index.html has no chrome; /blog/ai-agents/index.html does). So those routes have no usable visual reference: implement what platform-product.jsx intends and flag it rather than claiming a match. - Tag pages DO have chrome. Target DOM:

Articles tagged with: X

- 404.html has full chrome; body is just

+

. - Reproduce React artefacts verbatim rather than "fixing" them: class="... undefined" where a className prop is absent, a trailing space in an unfeatured solution item's class list,

wrapping an
  • , and

    ...

    from dangerouslySetInnerHTML excerpts. - The production bundle references --color-background-secondary, --color-text-light and --line-height-loose, none of which are ever defined, so those rules are inert on the live site too. Do not "fix" that. - Homepage Recent Articles uses the raw front-matter date in a
    ; /blog/ uses the formatted date in a

    . Reproduce both. - **Open parity risk (from PPY-6ee6aa):** production's .responsive-float-right-image{float:right;width:40%} targets the itself, but anthus_dom.image_html puts class_name on the wrapping div.gatsby-image-wrapper. Routing the about / ai-solutions images through it changes the DOM shape — probably visually equivalent, definitely not byte-identical. Eyeball it in bin/compare.py. - /ryan/ has THREE index-module--list--fb407 lists, not two; the first two are adjacent with zero characters between them, so a single {portfolio} hole must span both. ## Rebase against the concurrent URL agent: NOT ATTEMPTED A concurrent agent is doing URL/redirect work in the main /Users/home/Projects/Anth.us-Papyrus checkout, touching build_via_papyrus.py, anthus_content.py, anthus_pages.py and amplify.yml. Overlap with this branch is expected in build_via_papyrus.py and anthus_pages.py. The rebase onto the latest feature/anthus-papyrus-port has NOT been run. When it is: if a conflict is about URL shape rather than design, keep their version and say so rather than resolving by guessing. Emitting production-shaped hrefs here (above) was chosen partly to reduce that conflict surface. ## Not verified / not done - Nothing rendered, nothing screenshotted, no per-page parity evidence. - The build has not been run since the anthus_mdx.py changes; it will fail. - **Nothing deployed.** Staging (app d2hbn1ig6nqyhy, branch staging, https://staging.d2hbn1ig6nqyhy.amplifyapp.com) still serves the previous build. The three staging guards — noindex meta on every page, robots.txt Disallow: /, and the X-Robots-Tag: noindex header — were live and verified before this work and have NOT been re-checked. They must not regress. - PAPYRUS_PIN was NOT changed; amplify.yml still pins Papyrus at d0b00b3. If a future session wants a staging deploy before the Papyrus PR merges, it may temporarily pin the feature/markus-layout-parity SHA — mark it loudly in-file and in the PR, and move it to a develop SHA once that PR merges. - Constraints still in force: STAGING ONLY, no custom domain / domain association / Route 53 / DNS. AWS_PROFILE=legacy, account 335163751677, us-east-1. NEVER pass a production app id to a mutating call — d1ffh6ny5rvtl, d23d9f23lg9obr, d1od6t7lzbwanr. Content is out of scope (presentation only); do not change the submodule pin. ## Suggested order for the next session 1. Read web/WIP-DESIGN-PARITY.md. 2. Finish the Papyrus side (PPY-5aee133c) far enough to have the shell seams, and RUN THE PILOBOL.US PROOF — it gates everything, see that issue. 3. mv web/anthus_pages.py.new over web/anthus_pages.py, finish the TODO functions, write web/anthus_page_html.py (PPY-6ee6aa has the analysis). 4. Rewire web/build_via_papyrus.py per the checklist in the WIP notes. 5. Get the build green, then screenshot-compare before claiming anything.
